checked.comment: Stochastic K-armed bandit with all distributions on [0,1]. The known horizon T is used by the algorithm.
Anytime version of the same setting; the learner does not know T.
MOSS is not in the registry, so null is correct.
MOSS-anytime is not in the registry, so null is correct.
Theorem 2: per-arm bound E[N_a(T)] <= (ln T - ln ln T)/Kinf + O_T(1). The regime and the condition mu* in (0,1) are recorded correctly.
Theorem 3: R_T <= (K-1) + 44 sqrt(KT), for all T >= 1, anytime.
Theorem 4: E[N_a(T)] <= ln T/Kinf + O_T((ln T)^{6/7}). The remainder is recorded via C_a.

Proposition 7 restates the known MOSS bound (Audibert & Bubeck 2009). The paper says: 'We do not claim any improvement on the results themselves.' Under instruction 7 it belongs in cited_results, not results.
Proposition 9 restates the known anytime-MOSS result (Degenne & Perchet 2016) with a re-derived proof. It belongs in cited_results.
Same as r6: this is the augmented-exploration branch of Proposition 9, a restated prior result.

summary: The four main theorems on KL-UCB-Switch (distribution-free and distribution-dependent bounds, for the known-horizon and anytime versions) are extracted accurately: constants, conditions, settings and registry ids all match the source. The only issue is that the MOSS and MOSS-anytime bounds (Propositions 7 and 9) are listed under results. They are correctly flagged is_new=false, but the paper explicitly presents them as previously known results, so under the instructions they belong in cited_results.
